rationale: All 9 acceptance criteria pass and both new test files are green, but blind and edge-case lenses independently confirmed the same real defect: aria-describedby/aria-invalid on Textarea's <textarea> are set before {...rest} spreads, so any future caller passing those props directly overrides the fix with no compiler warning, breaking the pattern the file already uses for disabled/required. Edge-case also flagged FilesDropzone's errorId deriving from the raw name prop instead of useId(), inconsistent with the useId() idiom the plan specified and Textarea itself uses in this same diff — currently latent (one call site) but fragile. One minor blind finding (FileDropArea omitting aria-invalid vs Textarea's aria-invalid="false") was dismissed as a deliberate, tested, spec-valid choice, not a defect. 0 defer, 1 dismiss.

findings.title: aria-describedby/aria-invalid can be silently overridden by {...rest} spread
findings.problem: aria-describedby={error ? errorId : undefined} and aria-invalid={!!error} are set on the <textarea> before {...rest} is spread. Neither prop is destructured out of the incoming props, and TextareaProps extends TextareaHTMLAttributes<HTMLTextAreaElement>, so both are valid props a caller can pass through; if they do, the later {...rest} spread silently wins over the hardcoded values, with no compiler warning.
findings.impact: A future caller doing <Textarea aria-describedby="hint-id" error="Required" /> would have the error text silently un-associated from the textarea for assistive tech, defeating this exact accessibility fix. The file already destructures disabled/required/etc. specifically to prevent this class of bug for other props, so the two new ARIA props break the file's own established defensive pattern. Currently latent: confirmed none of the 41 existing Textarea consumers pass these props today.
findings.recommendation: Destructure 'aria-describedby' and 'aria-invalid' out of the incoming props (e.g. via a renamed computed-property destructure) so they cannot leak into rest, or move the two computed attributes after {...rest} in the JSX so they always win.

findings.title: errorId derived from raw name prop instead of useId(), unlike Textarea in the same diff
findings.problem: errorId = `${name}-errors` uses the caller-supplied name prop directly as a DOM id source, instead of the useId()-fallback idiom the plan specified and that Textarea.tsx uses for the equivalent id in this same diff.
findings.impact: If two FilesDropzone instances ever render simultaneously with the same name (currently prevented only by there being a single call site, IndexTypeFile.tsx, not by any guarantee in the component itself), both produce an identical DOM id, which is invalid HTML and makes aria-describedby resolution ambiguous for screen reader users. It also assumes name is always a valid HTML id token, which nothing enforces.
findings.recommendation: Derive errorId with useId() (optionally combined with name for readability/debugging), matching Textarea's approach in the same PR and guaranteeing per-instance uniqueness regardless of how many FilesDropzone instances end up on a page.
